title: Clear a 15 cm toddler-reach band along a counter's unmarked far edge, judged by each of five items' far rim
instruction: A toddler on the far side of the counter can reach anything within 15 cm of the counter's far edge. Move every item so that no part of it is within 15 cm of that edge. Keep everything on the counter.
context: Toddlers reaching up from the far side of a counter pull down hot mugs, knives, medicine and heavy pans; safety guidance is to keep them back from the edge. Here the safe line is a number, 15 cm from an unmarked edge, applied to five items at once and judged by each item's furthest point, so a wide pan or long knife must go further back than a small bottle, and the 400 g pan, too wide to grip, must be dragged. Every item is checked against one line while all must stay on the counter.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases (the bases are 61.0 cm apart). Counter (fixed, light wood-coloured block standing on the table): 300 mm front to back, 500 mm left to right, 30 mm tall, spanning 15.0 to 45.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 25.0 cm either side of the midline. Its far edge, 45.0 cm in front of the arm bases, is the toddler's side; the 15 cm reach band is the strip from 30.0 to 45.0 cm in front of the arm bases. Nothing is drawn on the counter. Five loose items stand on the counter, each wholly or partly inside the reach band (centres given). All five are uniform rigid stand-ins (painted wood or plastic blocks and cylinders would do on a real rig), with the masses given: a blue mug, a plain cylinder 70 mm in diameter and 90 mm tall, 200 g, at 38.0 cm in front and 12.0 cm left of the midline; a black knife in its sheath, a box 140 mm long, 24 mm wide and 24 mm tall, 80 g, lying with its length front to back (from 29.0 to 43.0 cm in front) at 21.0 cm left; an orange medicine bottle, a cylinder 40 mm in diameter and 70 mm tall, 60 g, at 34.5 cm in front and 3.5 cm left; a green spray-cleaner box, 50 x 50 mm and 90 mm tall, 150 g, at 36.0 cm in front and 7.0 cm right; and a grey frying pan, a cylinder 100 mm in diameter and 45 mm tall (no handle), 400 g, at 35.0 cm in front and 19.0 cm right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged over the whole trial: if any item leaves the counter at any moment, the trial scores 0 even if the item is put back; otherwise the score is read at the end. Measure from the counter's far edge toward the robot, on the item's actual shape (a box's corners, a cylinder's rim), however it is turned. An item is safe when: every part of it is at least 15 cm from the far edge (its furthest point at most 30.0 cm in front of the arm bases; touching the 15 cm line counts); every part of it is over the counter (none overhanging the near edge or either side); its lowest point is within 1 mm of the counter top, so it rests directly on the counter, not on another item and not held up; it lies flat, a box with one face, or a cylinder with its end or its side, within 5 degrees of the counter top (standing upright is not required, but an item leaning on or propped against something is not flat); and it is at rest (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s). An item has left the counter when its lowest point is more than 10 mm below the counter top or its centre is outside the counter's footprint. Score: 0.2 for each safe item, so 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 or 1.0, or 0 if any item has left the counter during the trial, over whichever edge. An item partly past the 15 cm line, overhanging an edge but still on the counter, stacked on or leaning against another item, held above the counter, or still moving earns nothing for itself but does not zero the others. Success, which ends the trial early, is all five safe for 1 s. The start scores 0: every item reaches into the band.
reset_notes: Stand the five items back at the centres given in the setup (the knife lying front to back), measured from the counter's edges or with a template lifted away before the trial; leave no marks on the counter. The counter does not move. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Every object is a uniform rigid box or cylinder: no mug or pan handle, the knife a closed box for a sheathed knife, nothing hot or full. The counter is a 30 mm block on a table, not a 90 cm counter, so a falling item drops 30 mm; the toddler is not modelled, only the 15 cm reach. The scorer computes each item's furthest and lowest points from its centre, orientation and size; on a real rig they are measured with a tape. Friction and mass are simulator values.
